bull.b: Affirm's shift from large losses in 2022–2024 to meaningful profitability in 2025–2026, with a reported 62.6% gross margin, marks a significant earnings inflection. Sustained operating leverage would strengthen resilience and provide more capacity to fund product growth internally.

TTM operating cash flow of $1.06B and free cash flow of $817M show that current profitability is translating into cash rather than remaining purely accounting-based. Positive internal cash generation can support funding flexibility and investment in distribution over the next several quarters.

An underwriting architecture that reportedly separates good from bad risk twice as well as the next traditional candidate could expand approvals by 2–3 points without incremental loss. Better risk selection can support volume, credit economics and merchant value over multiple quarters.

bear.b: Although the latest debt-to-equity ratio is about 0.20, it was about 1.79 in the 2026 annual report and above 2.0 in prior years. That history signals funding and capital-structure volatility, making current balance-sheet strength less proven through cycles.

Funding costs rose 27 basis points sequentially, while provision expense as a share of GMV and delinquencies also increased. Even if partly seasonal or tied to experiments, these trends can pressure margins and require disciplined underwriting as growth scales.

Direct-to-consumer growth through cards carries lower average interchange than integrated-merchant discount rates, reducing network revenue relative to GMV. A larger mix of this channel could therefore dilute monetization and make margin expansion more dependent on product mix.
